questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to the word 'ARDUOUS':
questions.explanation: ARDUOUS means requiring great effort, difficult and tiring. LABORIOUS means involving considerable effort — a close synonym. EFFORTLESS means easy, the opposite. ENJOYABLE means pleasant, unrelated to difficulty. LEISURELY means relaxed and unhurried, opposite in implication.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'BENEVOLENT':
questions.explanation: BENEVOLENT means well-meaning and kindly. MALEVOLENT means having or showing a wish to do evil — the direct antonym. GENEROUS is similar in meaning to benevolent. CHARITABLE is also similar. MERCIFUL means showing compassion, which is close to benevolent, not opposite.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about synonyms:

(i) 'Commence' and 'Begin' are synonyms.
(ii) 'Halt' and 'Continue' are synonyms.
(iii) 'Enormous' and 'Gigantic' are synonyms.
(iv) 'Serene' and 'Tranquil' are synonyms.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Commence and Begin both mean to start. (iii) is correct — Enormous and Gigantic both mean extremely large. (iv) is correct — Serene and Tranquil both mean calm and peaceful. (ii) is INCORRECT — Halt means to stop, while Continue means to go on; they are antonyms, not synonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Verbose' and 'Concise' are antonyms.
Reason (R): Verbose means using more words than necessary, while concise means giving information clearly and briefly.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — verbose (wordy/lengthy) and concise (brief/succinct) are antonyms. Reason (R) is correct — it accurately defines both words, showing they have opposite meanings. The definitions in (R) directly demonstrate WHY they are antonyms. Option B is wrong because the definitions explain the antonym relationship. Option C is wrong because (R) is factually correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their synonyms:

Column I:
(a) Diligent
(b) Prudent
(c) Affluent
(d) Obsolete

Column II:
(i) Wealthy
(ii) Outdated
(iii) Industrious
(iv) Cautious

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Diligent means hardworking/industrious (a-iii). Prudent means showing care and thought/cautious (b-iv). Affluent means having a great deal of money/wealthy (c-i). Obsolete means no longer in use/outdated (d-ii). Option B swaps diligent with prudent. Option C mismatches prudent with wealthy. Option D incorrectly pairs diligent with outdated.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs are correctly identified as ANTONYMS?

(i) Frugal — Extravagant
(ii) Timid — Bold
(iii) Vivid — Dull
(iv) Candid — Honest

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Frugal (thrifty) vs Extravagant (wasteful) — antonyms (i correct). Timid (shy/fearful) vs Bold (courageous) — antonyms (ii correct). Vivid (bright/intense) vs Dull (lacking brightness) — antonyms (iii correct). Candid (frank/open) and Honest (truthful) — these are SYNONYMS not antonyms (iv incorrect). Options B and D include (iv) which is a synonym pair.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'PRAGMATIC':
questions.explanation: PRAGMATIC means dealing with things sensibly and realistically, based on practical considerations. PRACTICAL is the closest synonym. IDEALISTIC means pursuing high or noble principles — often the antonym. THEORETICAL means based on theory rather than practice — opposite. VISIONARY means thinking about the future with imagination — opposite to pragmatic.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'EPHEMERAL':
questions.explanation: EPHEMERAL means lasting for a very short time. PERMANENT means lasting or intended to last indefinitely — the direct antonym. BRIEF means short in duration — similar to ephemeral. FLEETING means passing swiftly — a synonym. TRANSIENT means lasting only a short time — also a synonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about antonym pairs:

(i) 'Opaque' is the antonym of 'Transparent'.
(ii) 'Reluctant' is the antonym of 'Eager'.
(iii) 'Scarcity' is the antonym of 'Abundance'.
(iv) 'Arrogant' is the antonym of 'Modest'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four pairs are correct antonyms. Opaque (not transparent) vs Transparent (clear/see-through) — antonyms (i). Reluctant (unwilling) vs Eager (keen/enthusiastic) — antonyms (ii). Scarcity (shortage) vs Abundance (plenty) — antonyms (iii). Arrogant (having an exaggerated sense of importance) vs Modest (unassuming) — antonyms (iv).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Meticulous' and 'Careless' are antonyms.
Reason (R): A meticulous person pays great attention to detail, whereas a careless person shows insufficient attention.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — meticulous (very careful) and careless (lacking attention to detail) are antonyms. Reason (R) is correct — it provides the definitions that show their opposite meanings. The Reason demonstrates exactly WHY they are antonyms. Option B is wrong because (R) directly explains the antonym relationship. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'INEVITABLE':
questions.explanation: INEVITABLE means certain to happen, unable to be avoided or prevented. UNAVOIDABLE is the closest synonym. AVOIDABLE is the direct antonym. UNCERTAIN means not definitely known — opposite. IMPROBABLE means not likely to happen — contrary to inevitable.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their ANTONYMS:

Column I:
(a) Eloquent
(b) Optimistic
(c) Rigid
(d) Dormant

Column II:
(i) Active
(ii) Pessimistic
(iii) Flexible
(iv) Inarticulate

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Eloquent (fluent/persuasive in speech) is the antonym of Inarticulate (unable to express clearly) (a-iv). Optimistic (hopeful) is the antonym of Pessimistic (expecting the worst) (b-ii). Rigid (stiff/inflexible) is the antonym of Flexible (bendable/adaptable) (c-iii). Dormant (inactive/sleeping) is the antonym of Active (engaged/functioning) (d-i). Option B and C mismatch multiple pairs. Option D incorrectly pairs eloquent with flexible.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'GREGARIOUS':
questions.explanation: GREGARIOUS means fond of company, sociable. RECLUSIVE means avoiding the company of others — the direct antonym. SOCIABLE is a synonym of gregarious. FRIENDLY is similar in meaning. OUTGOING also means sociable — a synonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) 'Ambiguous' means having more than one possible meaning.
(ii) The synonym of 'Ambiguous' is 'Clear'.
(iii) 'Equivocal' is a synonym of 'Ambiguous'.
(iv) The antonym of 'Ambiguous' is 'Unambiguous' or 'Explicit'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation. Statement (iii) is correct — equivocal means open to interpretation, a synonym of ambiguous. Statement (iv) is correct — unambiguous/explicit mean clear and unequivocal, antonyms of ambiguous. Statement (ii) is INCORRECT — 'Clear' is an ANTONYM of ambiguous, not a synonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'OMINOUS':
questions.explanation: OMINOUS means giving the impression that something bad will happen; threatening. THREATENING is the closest synonym. AUSPICIOUS means indicating a good future — antonym. HARMLESS means not likely to cause harm — opposite implication. ENCOURAGING means giving hope — opposite.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct SYNONYM pairs?

(i) Magnanimous — Generous
(ii) Lethargic — Energetic
(iii) Novice — Beginner
(iv) Reticent — Reserved

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Magnanimous (generous/forgiving) and Generous are synonyms (i correct). Novice (a person new to something) and Beginner are synonyms (iii correct). Reticent (not revealing thoughts readily) and Reserved (slow to reveal feelings) are synonyms (iv correct). Lethargic (sluggish/lacking energy) and Energetic (full of energy) are ANTONYMS, not synonyms (ii incorrect).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'PROLIFIC':
questions.explanation: PROLIFIC means producing much fruit, foliage, or offspring; highly productive. UNPRODUCTIVE means not producing much — the direct antonym. FERTILE means capable of producing — similar to prolific. CREATIVE means having the ability to produce original ideas — similar. ABUNDANT means existing in large quantities — similar.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Altruistic' and 'Selfish' are antonyms.
Reason (R): Altruism involves selfless concern for others' well-being, while selfishness involves concern only for oneself.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — altruistic (unselfishly caring for others) and selfish (caring only for oneself) are antonyms. Reason (R) is correct — it defines both concepts and shows their opposite orientations. The definitions in (R) demonstrate the antonym relationship. Option B is wrong because (R) explains exactly why they are opposites. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The word 'MELANCHOLY' is most similar in meaning to __________.
questions.explanation: MELANCHOLY means a feeling of pensive sadness, often with no obvious cause. SADNESS is the closest synonym. HAPPINESS is the opposite — antonym. ANGER denotes a different emotion — irritation or rage. EXCITEMENT means a feeling of enthusiasm — unrelated and opposite in tone.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'CLANDESTINE':
questions.explanation: CLANDESTINE means kept secret or done secretively. SECRET is the closest synonym. OVERT means open and observable — antonym. OBVIOUS means easily seen — antonym. PUBLIC means open to all — antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their synonyms:

Column I:
(a) Gregarious
(b) Tenacious
(c) Voracious
(d) Audacious

Column II:
(i) Bold
(ii) Sociable
(iii) Greedy/Insatiable
(iv) Persistent

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Gregarious means fond of company/sociable (a-ii). Tenacious means holding fast/persistent (b-iv). Voracious means wanting large amounts/insatiable (c-iii). Audacious means showing bold willingness/bold (d-i). Option B swaps gregarious with tenacious. Option C mismixes tenacious and voracious. Option D mismatches gregarious with bold.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'LUCID':
questions.explanation: LUCID means expressed clearly, easy to understand. CONFUSED means lacking clarity or order — the antonym. CLEAR is a synonym of lucid. TRANSPARENT means easy to perceive — similar. INTELLIGIBLE means able to be understood — also a synonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the word 'PERNICIOUS':

(i) It means having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual way.
(ii) 'Beneficial' is its antonym.
(iii) 'Harmless' is its synonym.
(iv) 'Detrimental' is its synonym.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — pernicious means causing harm in a subtle way. Statement (ii) is correct — beneficial (helpful/advantageous) is its antonym. Statement (iv) is correct — detrimental (causing harm) is its synonym. Statement (iii) is INCORRECT — harmless means causing no harm, which is the opposite of pernicious, not a synonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'VENERATE':
questions.explanation: VENERATE means to regard with great respect. REVERE means to feel deep respect or admiration — a close synonym. DISRESPECT means to show lack of respect — antonym. IGNORE means to pay no attention — opposite. CONDEMN means to express strong disapproval — opposite.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Loquacious' is a synonym of 'Taciturn'.
Reason (R): Loquacious means tending to talk a great deal, while taciturn means reserved or saying little.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is INCORRECT — loquacious and taciturn are actually ANTONYMS, not synonyms. Loquacious means talkative while taciturn means silent/reserved — opposite meanings. Reason (R) is CORRECT — it accurately defines both words, showing they have opposite meanings. Option A is wrong because (A) is incorrect. Option B is wrong because (A) is incorrect. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'OSTENTATIOUS':
questions.explanation: OSTENTATIOUS means designed to impress, showy. MODEST means unassuming in the estimation of one's abilities — the antonym. FLASHY means ostentatiously attractive — a synonym. SHOWY means having a striking appearance — a synonym. PRETENTIOUS means attempting to impress by affecting importance — similar.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs are correctly identified as SYNONYMS?

(i) Cognizant — Aware
(ii) Benign — Malignant
(iii) Exquisite — Beautiful
(iv) Mundane — Ordinary

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Cognizant (having knowledge) and Aware (having knowledge of) — synonyms (i correct). Exquisite (extremely beautiful/delicate) and Beautiful — synonyms (iii correct). Mundane (lacking excitement/ordinary) and Ordinary — synonyms (iv correct). Benign (gentle/not harmful) and Malignant (evil/cancerous) — ANTONYMS, not synonyms (ii incorrect).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'PLAUSIBLE':
questions.explanation: PLAUSIBLE means seeming reasonable or probable. BELIEVABLE means able to be believed — the closest synonym. INCREDIBLE means difficult to believe — antonym. IMPOSSIBLE means not able to occur — antonym. DOUBTFUL means feeling uncertain — opposite.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about synonym-antonym relationships:

(i) 'Frugal' (thrifty) has 'Extravagant' as its antonym.
(ii) 'Succinct' (briefly expressed) has 'Verbose' as its antonym.
(iii) 'Pristine' (original condition) has 'Contaminated' as its antonym.
(iv) 'Amiable' (friendly) has 'Cordial' as its antonym.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — frugal (economical) vs extravagant (wasteful) are antonyms. Statement (ii) is correct — succinct (brief) vs verbose (wordy) are antonyms. Statement (iii) is correct — pristine (pure/unspoiled) vs contaminated (polluted) are antonyms. Statement (iv) is INCORRECT — amiable (friendly) and cordial (warm/friendly) are SYNONYMS, not antonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'MAGNANIMOUS':
questions.explanation: MAGNANIMOUS means generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival. PETTY means of little importance or narrow-minded — the antonym. GENEROUS is a synonym of magnanimous. NOBLE is similar in meaning. FORGIVING is also similar.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their ANTONYMS:

Column I:
(a) Tranquil
(b) Obscure
(c) Haughty
(d) Sporadic

Column II:
(i) Humble
(ii) Turbulent
(iii) Frequent
(iv) Famous

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Tranquil (calm/peaceful) is the antonym of Turbulent (characterized by conflict/disorder) (a-ii). Obscure (not well known) is the antonym of Famous (well known) (b-iv). Haughty (arrogantly superior) is the antonym of Humble (modest) (c-i). Sporadic (occurring irregularly) is the antonym of Frequent (occurring often) (d-iii). Option B swaps tranquil with obscure. Option C mismatches obscure with humble. Option D incorrectly pairs tranquil with humble.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'IMPECCABLE':
questions.explanation: IMPECCABLE means without faults or errors, perfect. FAULTLESS means free from defect — the closest synonym. FLAWED means having imperfections — antonym. MEDIOCRE means of average quality — opposite. DEFECTIVE means having faults — antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'PERTINENT':
questions.explanation: PERTINENT means relevant or applicable to a particular matter. IRRELEVANT means not connected or not applicable — the direct antonym. RELEVANT is a synonym of pertinent. APPROPRIATE means suitable — similar. APPLICABLE means relevant — similar.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the word 'UBIQUITOUS':

(i) It means present, appearing, or found everywhere.
(ii) 'Omnipresent' is its synonym.
(iii) 'Rare' is its antonym.
(iv) 'Common' is its antonym.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — ubiquitous means found everywhere. Statement (ii) is correct — omnipresent (present everywhere) is its synonym. Statement (iii) is correct — rare (seldom occurring/found) is its antonym. Statement (iv) is INCORRECT — 'common' means occurring frequently, which is closer to ubiquitous in meaning (though not a perfect synonym), not its antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'AVERSE':
questions.explanation: AVERSE means having a strong dislike or opposition to something. RELUCTANT means unwilling — the closest synonym. EAGER means keen or enthusiastic — antonym. WILLING means ready to do something — antonym. ENTHUSIASTIC means having intense enjoyment — antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The word 'PRECARIOUS' is most opposite in meaning to __________.
questions.explanation: PRECARIOUS means not securely held, in a dangerous state. SECURE means fixed/stable/free from danger — the antonym. DANGEROUS is similar to precarious. RISKY means involving the possibility of danger — similar. UNSTABLE means likely to change — similar.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'CANDID':
questions.explanation: CANDID means truthful and straightforward, frank. DECEPTIVE means giving an appearance or impression different from the truth — the antonym. FRANK is a synonym of candid. HONEST is a synonym. STRAIGHTFORWARD is also a synonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct ANTONYM pairs?

(i) Robust — Fragile
(ii) Concur — Disagree
(iii) Proximity — Distance
(iv) Apathy — Apathy

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Robust (strong/healthy) vs Fragile (easily broken/delicate) — antonyms (i correct). Concur (agree) vs Disagree — antonyms (ii correct). Proximity (nearness) vs Distance (remoteness) — antonyms (iii correct). Apathy vs Apathy — this is the SAME word repeated, not an antonym pair (iv incorrect). The antonym of apathy would be enthusiasm or passion.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'COPIOUS':
questions.explanation: COPIOUS means large in quantity, abundant. ABUNDANT means existing in great quantity — the closest synonym. SCANTY means insufficient in quantity — antonym. MEAGRE means lacking in quantity — antonym. LIMITED means restricted in amount — antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'VINDICATE':
questions.explanation: VINDICATE means to clear of blame or suspicion. ACCUSE means to charge with a fault or offence — the antonym. JUSTIFY means to show to be right — similar to vindicate. EXONERATE means to absolve from blame — synonym. ABSOLVE means to declare free from blame — synonym.
